[DAY1 20:31:30 - DAY1 20:31:59]
I put the takeout into the microwave. "I'll throw it in the microwave," I say. I turn off the microwave and head to the living room. "Strong insulation, hmm," I say. I talk with Lucia. Lucia: "Uh, which microwave are you using?" I ask, "How is it strong insulation?" Katrina: "What's up?" Lucia: "Nothing, just our takeout arrived." Katrina comes over and I look at her. We discuss it together. Lucia: "Haha, so we often just leave it in the microwave to keep warm." "Yeah, but this one doesn't," I say. I notice a rice cooker, take a bag, and put it into the rice cooker by the kitchen. Lucia: "Make the most of it, really."

[DAY1 20:32:00 - DAY1 20:32:29]
I can't get it in. Lucia asks, "Can it fit?" "Go in," I say. "It doesn't fit," I say and take it out. "But it's not a big problem," I add. "We have another one upstairs," I say. Lucia replies, "Oh, makes sense." I pick up a few things for tonight, then slowly walk up to the second floor, move to the corner, reach the living room doorway and walk in. I head to the kitchen, open the microwave, put a bag of food inside, close it, and turn toward the living room.

[DAY6 11:54:00 - DAY6 11:57:00]
I leave the living room and head toward Tasha’s room, noticing her packing clothes and discussing the use of lifelines and data cables with her. After confirming that Tasha is plugging in her own lifeline which is downstairs, I proceed downstairs, pick up a data cable, and wear it around my neck before exiting the house into the yard where Shure is standing. I engage briefly with Katrina, who shows me something on her phone, then re-enter the house and move through the living room to the courtyard, interacting with Tasha about decorative "paper eyes" that can be stuck on objects to give them a "soulful" quality.

I continue organizing data cables while Tasha decorates my phone case with the small circular parts, discussing whose cables belong to whom and noting the markings on them. After exchanging cables verbally with Tasha and observing her handiwork on my phone, I walk toward the door, reiterate a shared ownership of cables, and hand a cable to Katrina. Passing Shure by the refrigerator, I comment on leftover Angus thick beef burgers that have not been eaten, and discuss with Shure and Alice whether to fry or microwave them, with Shure deciding on microwaving. Finally, I respond to Katrina’s question about charging a device directly, confirming that it is possible.
